July Climate Snapshot
Tokyo in July experiences hot, humid summer conditions with average highs around 29-30°C and lows near 23°C, high relative humidity often exceeding 75%, and substantial rainfall averaging 150-200mm over about 12-15 rainy days. Sydney in July, being winter, has mild temperatures with average highs of 17-18°C and lows around 8-9°C, lower humidity typically 50-65%, and minimal rainfall of about 80-100mm spread over 7-10 days.

Historical July Climate Comparison
| Metric | Tokyo, Japan | Sydney, Australia |
|--------|--------------|-------------------|
| Avg High Temp (°C) | 29-30 | 17-18 |
| Avg Low Temp (°C) | 23 | 8-9 |
| Avg Humidity (%) | 75-85 | 50-65 |
| Avg Rainfall (mm) | 150-200 | 80-100 |
| Rainy Days | 12-15 | 7-10 |

Travel Comfort for Heat-Induced Asthma
Sydney is more suitable for a traveler with heat-induced asthma. Tokyo's July heat (above 25°C with high humidity) can trigger asthma symptoms by increasing airway inflammation and breathing difficulty, while Sydney's cooler, drier winter conditions reduce these risks despite occasional light rain.

Context for July Data
Tokyo data reflects its humid subtropical climate during peak rainy season (tsuyu ending early July), drawing from long-term averages; Sydney's figures are from its temperate oceanic winter, with less variability. Data synthesized from climate charts; minor variations exist by source due to station locations.
